title: JWT Basics
description: Learn to use JWT tokens for API authentication.

data.text: **JWT (JSON Web Tokens)** are compact, URL-safe tokens used for authentication in stateless APIs.

data.caption: A JWT is composed of three dot-separated parts
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    A[Header] --> B[.]
    B --> C[Payload]
    C --> D[.]
    D --> E[Signature]
    E --> F[Token]

terms.definition: Claims containing user data and expiration
Verifies the token has not been tampered with
A statement about the user, such as name or role

data.title: Validating JWT

items: Header: Token type and signing algorithm

data.title: Tip
data.text: Always use HTTPS in production so JWTs cannot be intercepted.

data.title: Inspect a JWT Token
data.description: Decode a sample JWT and examine its three parts without verifying the signature.
steps: Find a sample JWT from jwt.io or your API
Read the claims in the payload
data.expectedOutcome: You will see the header and payload structure and understand what claims are stored.

items.text: Know the three parts of a JWT
Can explain why JWTs are stateless
Can configure JWT bearer validation in ASP.NET Core

data.title: Key Takeaways
data.takeaway: JWTs are the standard for modern API authentication.
